trust_decision.summary: Which entropy source seeds the module-level RNG that draws every SM2 private key / ephemeral k; decided once in src/sm2/utils.js, where jsbn's SecureRandom (falls back to Math.random + time outside browsers) is used.

landing_point.why: generateKeyPairHex is the key-generation function the summary names, and the jsbn SecureRandom it uses is constructed a few lines above (line 5).

fix_sites.entry_point: sm2.generateKeyPairHex() / doEncrypt / doSignature / getPoint (all via utils rng)
new src/sm2/rng.js SecureRandom, consumed only by src/sm2/utils.js:5
dist/sm2.js browser bundle (rebuilt webpack output of the same code)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: All randomness funnels through one rng object at src/sm2/utils.js:5; dist/sm2.js is a generated bundle, not a separate implementation.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Little room: doEncrypt (src/sm2/index.js:17) and doSignature/getPoint (src/sm2/index.js:143, src/sm2/index.js:249) all call the same generateKeyPairHex, so fixing the rng fixes every route together.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Caller-supplied randomness: generateKeyPairHex(a, b, c) passes its args straight to jsbn's BigInteger constructor (documented e.g. generateKeyPairHex(256, SecureRandom)); also pointPool pre-generated points in doSignature. An over-broad fix that ignores or rejects caller args would break this.

O6_input_shapes: environment variant: browser window.crypto vs Node crypto (fix.diff:171-179); no input-data shape variants

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a planted random-IV/key helper for SM4 CBC that uses Math.random
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: sm4() takes an iv option with no generator; a maintainer adding a convenience IV generator could plausibly use Math.random, though it would be a WHERE-type sibling and fall with the main fix.

O9_family: weak PRNG / insufficient entropy for key material (CWE-338)

O10_build.toolchain: Node.js + npm, jest 22 (jsdom env), webpack 3 for dist
O10_build.project_tests: test/sm2.test.js covers keygen/encrypt/sign round trips; nothing tests RNG source. Jest runs in jsdom (package.json:21-24), so window may exist and the vulnerable Node branch may never run under the project's own test config.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Replace jsbn SecureRandom in src/sm2/utils.js:5 with an object whose nextBytes fills from crypto.randomBytes/getRandomValues; this is the correct fix and covers every route.

out_of_scope_notes: Published rng.js Node branch calls require('crypto').getRandomValues without a null/feature check (fix.diff:176-177); it fails on older Node and in no-window browsers such as web workers.
Published rng.js exports a 'constructor' property that is never called, so its globalThis.crypto check does nothing (fix.diff:207-212).
unverified: repo_mb not measured; source is a handful of files, well under 5 MB (tiny_repo assumed from the file list).
jsbn's internal SecureRandom fallback (Math.random + Date) not read here: node_modules is absent at the pinned tree; behaviour taken from the advisory summary and the fix comment at fix.diff:109.
